items.description: Give locally reviewed no-action findings a delivery path.
evidence: .agents/steering/lifecycle.md:36 moves an approved review to review-findings when it requests changes.
.agents/steering/lifecycle.md:40 restores only a committed target after all findings are terminally no-action.
items.analysis: A local review can request changes and have every finding declined, skipped, deferred, or otherwise settled. That target was never committed, so Resolve cannot restore a delivery state or send it to commit. The workflow remains triaged despite having no remaining action.
items.recommendation: Define the no-action exit for a locally reviewed target: restore it to approved with next commit, while preserving committed targets as committed and directing them to complete.
items.decision_rationale: This is the earlier no-action lifecycle exit adapted for delivery: locally reviewed work returns to approved, then enters commit rather than completing directly.

dispatch.reason: Resolve now restores local no-action review to approved with next commit.

items.description: Allow submitted normal changes to re-enter verification without replacing current work.
evidence: .agents/steering/lifecycle.md:40 promises that committed normal changes return through verification, review, approval, and commit.
.agents/skills/verify/SKILL.md:22 permits named non-active verification only for bugfix and refactor targets.
items.analysis: A submitted normal change that receives external feedback can be triaged while another issue is active, but cannot take the documented verification step after a fix because Verify rejects named non-active normal work. This blocks the promised feedback loop.
items.recommendation: Extend the named non-active workflow guards and lifecycle rules to support committed normal targets through build, verification, review, approval, and recommit without replacing the active issue.
items.decision_rationale: Submitted normal changes must be repairable and redeliverable without disrupting the active issue.

dispatch.reason: Named committed normal targets can now resume build, verification, review, approval, and commit in place.

items.description: Update the root lifecycle reference for the delivery workflow.
evidence: LIFECYCLE.md:5 says approved, committed, commit, and complete are planned and unimplemented.
LIFECYCLE.md:78 shows review approval leading directly to complete.
items.analysis: The root reference and diagrams contradict the active steering policy and the delivered skills. README directs readers to this document, so people following the repository documentation receive an obsolete workflow.
items.recommendation: Revise LIFECYCLE.md to match the implemented delivery states, transitions, command ownership, and vertical flow diagrams.
items.decision_rationale: The repository lifecycle reference and diagrams must describe the delivery workflow now implemented by this change.

dispatch.reason: The root lifecycle reference and diagrams now describe the delivery workflow.

items.description: Reconcile SCHEMA.md with the installed distribution and delivery records.
evidence: SCHEMA.md:16 names src/specle/skills and src/specle/steering instead of src/specle/blueprints/.
SCHEMA.md:24 says every .agents file is Markdown despite the generated skills/specle/index.json resource.
SCHEMA.md:53-60 omits the planned versioned delivery-record contract.
items.analysis: The schema reference describes superseded inventory locations and an obsolete Markdown-only rule, and it has no place for the delivery record required by the new commit and complete workflow.
items.recommendation: Update SCHEMA.md for the blueprint layout, generated-index exception, and the delivery evidence currently stored in the selected context record. Do not make the delivery workflow wait for a separate future schema change.
items.decision_rationale: The layout and generated-resource documentation must match the installed distribution now. Delivery evidence belongs in the selected target's existing context record; a future schema change is not a prerequisite.

dispatch.reason: SCHEMA.md now names the blueprint layout, generated-index exception, and current context-record delivery evidence without deferring this workflow to future schema work.

items.description: Correct only stale README references owned by the repository introduction.
evidence: README.md:21 directs readers to the obsolete root LIFECYCLE.md.
README.md:7-21 does not describe local approval, delivery policy, commit, committed, or complete.
items.analysis: The README should remain a concise introduction. Dedicated lifecycle, schema, and project-policy documents own workflow detail. Once those references are current, README needs only any directly stale path or link correction it owns.
items.recommendation: Correct only stale README references or paths. Do not add a delivery-policy overview or duplicate the dedicated documentation.
items.decision_rationale: Keep README concise; fix only inaccuracies in its own links or paths and leave policy detail to dedicated documents.

dispatch.reason: README remained concise because its lifecycle link is valid after the root lifecycle reference was corrected.

items.description: Preserve committed state in root lifecycle no-action diagrams.
evidence: LIFECYCLE.md:88 routes committed external feedback to review-findings.
LIFECYCLE.md:94 routes every triaged no-action result to approved.
LIFECYCLE.md:110 and LIFECYCLE.md:116 repeat the same path for abbreviated work.
items.analysis: The root diagrams collapse local-review and submitted-feedback origins. A committed pull request with no actionable external findings must return to committed and then complete, but the diagram sends it to approved and would require recommitting an unchanged delivery.
items.recommendation: Split the no-action transition by origin in both diagrams: local review returns to approved; external feedback on a committed delivery returns to committed.
items.decision_rationale: Authoritative Resolve and steering already restore submitted no-action work to committed; the root diagrams must match that behaviour.

dispatch.reason: The revised contract and plan now distinguish local and committed no-action origins.

items.description: Do not complete an independent-spec hand-off before delivery.
evidence: src/specle/blueprints/skills/resolve/SKILL.md:25 directs Resolve to complete an active normal target before creating an independent spec.
src/specle/blueprints/skills/resolve/SKILL.md:27 correctly says only an evidenced configured delivery outcome may complete a target.
items.analysis: The independent-spec route still contains the pre-delivery lifecycle rule. A locally approved change whose finding is routed to a new independent spec would be marked complete without its configured commit or pull-request delivery event, contradicting the delivery policy.
items.recommendation: Keep the origin at approved or committed according to its delivery history after recording the independent-spec hand-off; require commit or complete for its own final delivery event.
items.decision_rationale: Independent work hand-off remains valid, but the delivery extension means it must preserve the origin's approved or committed state rather than completing it.

dispatch.reason: The revised contract and plan preserve origin delivery state during independent-spec hand-off.

items.description: Deliver coupled approved sidecars with their active change in one commit.
evidence: .specle/context.json records the active delivery-policy change and queued prevent-assumed-dependencies bugfix as approved with next commit.
src/specle/blueprints/skills/commit/SKILL.md:18-20 selects one target and prohibits including unrelated work.
src/specle/blueprints/skills/commit/SKILL.md:26 preserves a non-active target but does not define a joint delivery transition.
items.analysis: The approved bugfix was intentionally layered onto the uncommitted active change and the user requires one commit. The current one-target commit rule either leaves the bugfix approved after its code is delivered or requires an artificial second commit. Neither outcome records the real delivery unit.
items.recommendation: Record the explicit origin and delivery relationship when a bugfix is raised from active work. `status` and `commit` use that declared relationship to include the related approved bugfix with its origin; do not infer membership from worktree overlap.
items.decision_rationale: A bugfix raised because active work is procedurally blocked must be linked to that work at creation. The explicit sidecar relationship, rather than a general inferred delivery set, determines joint delivery.

dispatch.reason: The delivery-policy plan now records explicit sidecar origin and delivery relationships, with no inferred worktree membership.
